title: Playing a tune first as a waltz then in 4/4, as Thomas does
summary: Asked about Thomas's habit of playing a tune as a waltz and then in 4/4, Barnes says it is not really right for every tune.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Speaking about playing dances, I noticed Thomas often, he'll play a tune, what was it called? You know, he'll say it's a waltz, and he'll play waltz time for several choruses. Then he'll stop, then right away pick it up in 4-4 time, play the same tune in 4-4 time again. Is that a usual thing in New Orleans?

Well, I'll tell you how it is. It goes to rise if you want. Yeah. But we'd do it like when it's a lead band, I don't say we. A man would do it, would play that waltz. They'd clap it and they'd play a waltz back. Then if you like sitting down, you'll pick it up. Pick it up and give it to them, oh, well this is short enough, let it go. And that time you don't do nothing. Now, you've got some waltzes pretty hard to play, like the waltzes, same for me and all them waltzes there, that's hard, that's broken time. You see, it's hard for you to pick up on waltz right there, to change the time of it, temporarily. But he plays it that way, because he didn't have it up to him, that's all I can say.
Yeah, it's just sort of a little habit of his. It goes over pretty good, but people like it pretty well.
Yeah, but it's not right when everyone wants to play. It'd go good in some ways.
Not all of them, you see?
